beat_player.text: Your formation cost you {troop_count} men. A proper cavalry wing would have prevented it.
Your centre broke, {player}. Bring more horse next time, or stop bringing me {troop_count} infantry.
Good fight, {player}. Your archers were badly placed, though. I took {gold} gold from your baggage train and you did not notice.
{troop_count} of your soldiers fell in that exchange, {player}. Recruit more cavalry and spend less on archers.

beat_by_player.text: My archers were out of position, {player}. Logistics, not skill. Those {troop_count} men were avoidable.
Your flanking was sound, {player}. My left wing had {troop_count} spearmen and no horse. That will be corrected.
Well played, {player}. I misjudged your second wave. I will take the lesson and recalculate before our next meeting.
{player} won that fight through ground and timing, not numbers. I will not repeat the error with {troop_count} men.

beat_by_player_repeat.text: That is the third time {player} has broken my line. The numbers say I should have won. I will find where the model is wrong.
{player}, I have reviewed every report. Three defeats, {troop_count} men lost each time. This is no longer chance.
{player} has now beaten me three times. Grudging respect is noted. Your cavalry ratio is higher than I predicted.
{player}, you have beaten me three times and I am beginning to take your formations seriously. Respect, grudgingly.

player_win_streak.text: {player} has won again. Every field is a problem for lesser commanders now. Mine included, and I dislike that.
Your streak is impressive, {player}. It will end when your supply lines do. Plan for that.
A long run of wins for {player}. Statistically this is a pattern, not luck. Study it.
Enjoy the streak, {player}. Every commander who rode one has eventually met a flank they did not expect.

player_big_defeat.text: {player} lost most of an army to someone else. {troop_count} men gone in one afternoon. Recruits are not free, {player}.
A rough day, {player}. You lost {troop_count} men, most of them to a bad formation. Rebuild the horse before you push again.
{player} just lost {troop_count} troops. Anyone who fields that much infantry deserves the result.
Your army broke, {player}. Do not chase the losses. Reorganise before you commit again.

whisper_challenge.text: {player}, I will be at {town} with cavalry. Meet me at {village} and we will see whose formation holds.
I would like a formal test of formations, {player}. {village} is neutral ground. Your move.
{player}, your record is fortunate. I propose we end that at {village}, outside {town}. Bring everything you have.
A calculated proposal, {player}. Your army against mine near {town}. Let us see which of us wastes fewer men.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work on that flank, {player}. Your horse held against {enemy_faction} as I expected. Do that again and we will get along.
Our combined line beat {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} men. The ratios were correct. Keep your cavalry where it was.
{player} and I took the field from {enemy_faction} with {troop_count} men. Adequate coordination.
Your timing was tolerable, {player}. Next time send the horse wide before the infantry closes. {enemy_faction} will not recover quickly.

ambient_brag.text: I hold {troop_count} men and {gold} gold, and {fief} is proof that my formations work.
Another {fief} secured. Cavalry-heavy armies do not lose ground, and I do not intend to start.
{gold} gold in the treasury and {troop_count} horse in the field. Recruiting properly is not complicated.

my_faction_took_fief.text: {fief} has fallen to {my_faction}. {enemy_faction} lost it because they fielded too much infantry.
{my_faction} now holds {fief}. The garrison will be cavalry, as it should be.
{fief} is ours. {enemy_faction} lost the flank before the walls ever mattered.

player_besieging_my_fief.text: {player} has started a siege of {fief}. Good. I have been waiting for someone to test the garrison.
{player}, {fief} is not a soft target. My garrison is cavalry. Your siege engines will not change that.
You have chosen {fief} to besiege, {player}. A calculated risk. I have run the odds and I am not worried.
{player} is besieging {fief}. Most sieges fail in the second week from supply shortfall. Count your provisions.

ambient_chatter.text: The road between {town} and {village} has been muddy for three days. Terrible for horse, which is why I stay off it.
Anyone still fielding a pure infantry army should reconsider. The numbers do not lie.
Lag at {village} again. I have stopped blaming the server and started blaming the weather.
Rain over {town} this week. My archers were out of position in the damp. Not an excuse, a variable.
Someone asked me for tactics at {village} yesterday. I charged them for it. Coaching is not free.
